ALL 66 are dropped from the findings stream under Law 3 - the owner is trusted for knowing actions, and 'a malicious owner could...' is pure noise. The suppression is recorded here rather than silently: any NON-OBVIOUS owner footgun in this same surface remains in scope and must still be raised by the reasoning agents (econ-scanner, story-faithfulness), which do not inherit this filter. Known-issue #1 already documents owner control of setTargetAPY / setDispatcherIndex / setNFTMinter / setDispatcherHook / setStakedId / topUp / pullAndRefresh as by-design.

Retained in the stream as raw tool output for traceability only; the prior refutation stands (NFTMinterV2._executeMint returns unconditional true or reverts). No new evidence.

Aderyn 'nonReentrant is Not the First Modifier' now fires at 4 sites and each was checked from source rather than closed by reference. InPlaceNFTStakerMigrator.sol:219 (migrateOut) and :253 (migrateIn) and NFTStakerMigrator.sol:170 (migrate) are all `onlyOwner nonReentrant`, and OZ Ownable._checkOwner is an owner() SLOAD plus revert with no external call. BatchNFTMinterMultiToken.sol:300 (batchMint) is `whenNotPaused nonReentrant`, where whenNotPaused is OZ Pausable reading the local _paused bool - the contract imports pauser/IPausable only to EXPOSE pause()/unpause() to a registered pauser address, and never calls out to a Pauser contract inside the modifier. No external call precedes the arming of _status at any of the 4 sites, so there is no reentrancy window. Kept in the stream at potential-low for the record.

escalationCandidates.observation: rewardTokens is a fully caller-supplied address[] and the ONLY exclusion applied is `rewardToken == paymentToken`. Any other ERC20 held by this contract can be named by any caller who clears the `count >= nudgeSize` threshold, and its ENTIRE balance is safeTransfer-ed to a caller-chosen recipient.
escalationCandidates.why: Deterministically visible from the code; whether this is a vulnerability or the intended nudge mechanic is an economic/spec question this stage cannot settle. Flagged for econ-scanner and story-faithfulness rather than dropped (Law 1 recall).

escalationCandidates.observation: The dust sweep is gated on `remaining / DUST_THRESHOLD != 0`; below the threshold the residue is retained AND totalPaid is reported as the full paymentAmount. Payment token is barred from rewardTokens, so retained residue is recoverable only via owner rescueERC20.
escalationCandidates.why: Return-value and accounting drift on a new contract - Low/QA at most, but it should reach the dedup stage rather than die here.

escalationCandidates.observation: The story-023 settlement-capture forwarding sequence is duplicated verbatim across the two migrators (self-documented as plan decision D-6, guarding against the pns20h1 fork drift). Confirmed line-for-line identical at this commit, including the `require(captured <= owed)` bound and both failure branches of the raw transfer try/catch.
escalationCandidates.why: Not a finding today - recorded as a DRIFT WATCH. Any future fix applied to one copy but not mirrored to the other re-creates the pns20h1 class. The next run must diff both bodies.
escalationCandidates.toolBasis: aderyn 'Unsafe ERC20 Operation' at :227 and :324 - both are the DELIBERATE raw transfer (SafeERC20 would revert and defeat the catch on non-reverting-false tokens). The detector is correct that the call is raw; the design rationale is sound and documented. Not escalated as an unsafe-transfer bug.

escalationCandidates.observation: The sole slither/reentrancy-no-eth hit on a changed file. Read from source: parked[user]=0, delete migrationBegin[user], totalParked -= amt and _removeParked(user) all precede _depositForAndForward (strict CEI), and the function is nonReentrant plus onlyOwner.
escalationCandidates.why: Appears clean; surfaced so dedup and code-scanner can confirm the CEI claim independently rather than inheriting this stage's read.
